section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study examining how body image-related cognitive fusion and body appreciation mediate the relationship between body image discrepancy and disordered eating behaviors, while controlling for BMI. The study involved a sample of women from the general population and found that the tested model explained 67% of eating psychopathology variance. The authors acknowledge key limitations including the cross-sectional design, exclusive focus on female participants, reliance on self-report measures, and the need for future longitudinal and clinical sample research.

section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study examining how body image-related cognitive fusion and body appreciation mediate the relationship between body image discrepancy and eating psychopathology (EDE-Q), while controlling for BMI. The path model explained 67% of eating psychopathology variance, with results indicating that body image discrepancy has both direct and indirect effects on disordered eating through these mediating mechanisms. The authors acknowledge limitations including the cross-sectional design, exclusive female sample from the general population, and reliance on self-report measures.
